task.title: A shopping note

instructions: Make sure you cover all of the points below.

required_points: how much money he can use

learning_objectives.text: Write a short note with simple instructions, quantities and a money limit

difficulty.language_demand: Short, concrete sentences about familiar personal topics; high-frequency vocabulary; present simple.
expected_performance: Addresses most of the required points with at least one simple sentence each; meaning is clear even with errors.
Correct simple present sentences with basic word order; some errors in agreement or articles do not stop understanding.
Uses basic words correctly for the topic (family, food, daily life); spelling of common words mostly correct.
difficulty.rationale: Heuristic components (0=A1 .. 5=C2): {'grammar': 0.5, 'cognition': 1.0, 'length': 0.0, 'abstractness': 0.5, 'prompt_language': 0.0}; composite 0.47 -> A1. Original target A1. Computed from invited grammar, cognitive operations, expected length, abstractness and prompt language only.

criteria.name: Task fulfilment
criteria.description: How fully and appropriately the response does what the task asks: required points, purpose, audience and, where relevant, position.
criteria.successful_performance: Addresses most of the required points with at least one simple sentence each; meaning is clear even with errors. Required points: three things to buy; how many of each; how much money he can use
criteria.weak_performance: Only one or two points, or sentences unrelated to the task; meaning often unclear.
criteria.expected_evidence: Which required points are present; how each is supported; whether purpose, audience and position are clear. Check each required point: three things to buy; how many of each; how much money he can use.
criteria.evaluation_limitations: Content knowledge is not assessed; do not penalise factual inaccuracy unless the task asks for accuracy to a supplied source.

criteria.name: Grammatical range and accuracy
criteria.description: Range of structures used and the accuracy with which they are controlled, including punctuation that affects clarity.
criteria.successful_performance: Correct simple present sentences with basic word order; some errors in agreement or articles do not stop understanding.
criteria.weak_performance: Fragments; missing verbs; frequent word-order errors.
criteria.expected_evidence: Types of structures; proportion of error-free sentences; kinds of errors; whether errors are systematic. Structures invited by the task: word_order, quantifiers.
criteria.evaluation_limitations: Judge by the structures the learner chooses and controls; do not penalise absence of structures the task does not invite.

patterns: missing 'be' in present sentences (Arabic nominal sentences)
l1_transfer_hypotheses.caution: These are hypotheses about common patterns; they are NOT to be reported as a learner weakness from a single instance.

criteria.name: Lexical resource
criteria.description: Range, precision and appropriateness of vocabulary, including collocation and word formation.
criteria.successful_performance: Uses basic words correctly for the topic (family, food, daily life); spelling of common words mostly correct.
criteria.weak_performance: Very few words; repeated copying; wrong or invented words.
criteria.expected_evidence: Range of topic words; repetition; collocation; word formation; spelling. Expected vocabulary demands: food and shop words; numbers; money.
criteria.evaluation_limitations: Do not reward unusual words that are used incorrectly; do not penalise a plain word that is correct and appropriate.

patterns: missing 'be' in present sentences (Arabic nominal sentences)
l1_transfer_hypotheses.caution: These are hypotheses about common patterns; they are NOT to be reported as a learner weakness from a single instance.

criteria.name: Coherence and cohesion
criteria.description: How logically the ideas connect and how clearly linking devices and reference express those connections.
criteria.successful_performance: Sentences are in a sensible order; simple linking such as 'and' and 'but' is used correctly.
criteria.weak_performance: Sentences appear in random order; no linking.
criteria.expected_evidence: Order of ideas; variety and accuracy of linkers; clarity of pronoun reference; paragraph logic.
criteria.evaluation_limitations: A text can be cohesive and still weak on content; keep this criterion separate from task fulfilment.

criteria.name: Register and appropriateness
criteria.description: Whether tone, formality, conventions of text type and politeness suit the audience and purpose.
criteria.successful_performance: Greeting and ending suitable for a simple message. Audience: your brother. Register: informal, simple
criteria.weak_performance: No greeting or ending where expected.
criteria.expected_evidence: Greeting/closing; politeness markers; formality of vocabulary and structures; conventions.
criteria.evaluation_limitations: Only scored where the task defines an audience/register; otherwise treat as not applicable.

policy.observed_error_vs_weakness: A diagnostic category is an OBSERVED error pattern when at least one instance is found in a response. It may be reported as an INFERRED learning weakness only after >= 3 instances in one response set of >= 100 words (or >= 2 responses) and when the error is not explained by task demands (for example a tense the task did not invite).

diagnostics.observed_vs_inferred: An error is OBSERVED when an instance appears in the response. It may be recorded as an INFERRED weakness only under the policy in diagnostics.policy (repeated instances, enough text, and not explained by task demands).
